strings.title: Ashes of Warehouse 12
strings.hint: The stopped watch does not lie: when did he really die? And who increased the insurance coverage ten days before the fire?
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: warehouse owner Rashad Qablan.

He killed his partner Munir a full week before the fire during an argument over concealed profits, then hid the body among the furniture in Warehouse 12 while looking for a way out. An ugly plan followed: an "electrical" fire would consume the body and the evidence and yield an insurance payout he had increased ten days earlier. But the fire betrayed him twice. It left enough of the body for an autopsy to establish that death had preceded the fire by days, and it left Munir's wristwatch, stopped at the true moment of his death, a full seven days before the fire.

The decomposition timeline, a gasoline receipt charged to his card on the night of the fire, and the recently increased insurance policy proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: A nighttime fire consumed Warehouse 12 in the warehouse district. The initial civil defense report gave the usual explanation: "electrical short circuit." But a charred body among the ashes changed everything, and the forensic morgue delivered a surprise: the man had died about a week before the fire. The fire killed no one that night. Its job was burial.
strings.summary.photoCap: The victim's wristwatch — stopped a week before the fire
strings.summary.victim.name: Munir Abboud
strings.summary.victim.job: Furniture business partner — reported missing 6 days earlier
strings.summary.victim.note: His disappearance was reported before the fire. The body solved the first mystery and opened the second.
strings.summary.timeline[0].l: Munir's last sighting — and his watch stops
strings.summary.timeline[3].l: The body is found among the ashes
strings.scene.intro: A single ignition point "coincidentally" beside the warehouse's oldest wiring, with accelerant (gasoline) specifically around the body: the fire was after a body, not a warehouse. The body had already been hidden behind a wall of stacked cabinets.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The victim's belongings recovered from the ashes
strings.scene.photos[1].cap: Warehouse 12 — after the fire was extinguished
strings.scene.notes[0]: Accelerant found only around the body
strings.scene.notes[1]: Death preceded the fire by 6-8 days
strings.scene.notes[2]: The body was hidden behind deliberately stacked cabinets
strings.scene.notes[3]: Insurance coverage was increased 10 days earlier
strings.evidence[0].title: The Stopped Wristwatch
strings.evidence[0].desc: Stopped by an impact seven days before the fire. The true moment of death was recorded mechanically.
strings.evidence[1].title: Decomposition Report
strings.evidence[1].desc: Death preceded the fire by a week. A fatal skull fracture caused by a hard object had nothing to do with the flames.
strings.evidence[2].title: Gasoline Receipt
strings.evidence[2].desc: 20 liters in two cans, paid for with Rashad Qablan's card three hours before the fire.
strings.evidence[3].title: Insurance Policy
strings.evidence[3].desc: Its value was increased 3 times over 10 days earlier, between the disappearance and the fire.
strings.evidence[4].title: The Double Profit Ledger
strings.evidence[4].desc: Two parallel sets of accounts, official and secret: the partners' concealed dispute.
strings.evidence[5].title: The Guard's Switched-Off Phone
strings.evidence[5].desc: The warehouse guard vanished on the night of the fire. An obvious suspect, or a fleeing witness?
strings.suspects[0].name: Rashad Qablan
strings.suspects[0].relation: A 15-year partnership and a dispute over profits
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "On the night of the fire I was at a family dinner. On the night he disappeared, I was at an exhibition outside the city."
strings.suspects[0].statement: Munir was my brother and partner. I reported my concern even before his wife did. I increased the insurance because stock doubled before the season: business, not crime. The gasoline was for the exhibition generator… I usually keep receipts, but that one went missing.
strings.suspects[1].name: Jomaa, the Missing Guard
strings.suspects[1].relation: Vanished on the night of the fire
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I ran because I was afraid of being accused. I saw something I shouldn't have." (After his arrest)
strings.suspects[1].statement: A week earlier, I heard an argument and something falling in Warehouse 12. I saw Mr. Rashad come out alone, terrified. He threatened my livelihood, so I kept quiet. On the night of the fire I saw him enter with two cans… and I ran before they could pin it on me.
strings.suspects[2].name: Wahid, the Insurance Broker
strings.suspects[2].relation: Arranged the coverage increase and earned a commission
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I handle paperwork. My commission is legal and recorded."
strings.suspects[2].statement: I suggested increasing the coverage because the client suddenly requested "greater protection," which is his right. Did I find the timing strange? Perhaps. Did I report it? No. Suspicion is not a crime and commission is not evidence.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Victim's wife
strings.witnesses[0].statement: In his last call, he told me: "I'm going to confront Rashad about the second ledger, then I'll be back." He never came back.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Gas Station Attendant
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I filled both cans myself. He was in a hurry and said on the phone: "Tonight, everything will be finished."
strings.witnesses[2].name: Owner of Warehouse 11
strings.witnesses[2].statement: A week before the fire, we noticed a strange smell and told Rashad. He said: "A dead rat. I'll deal with it." And he did… with fire.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Missing-Person and Fire Reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: Munir was reported missing 6 days earlier, followed by the fire report for Warehouse 12. Both were combined into one file after the autopsy.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Fire Origin Report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Petroleum accelerant around the body and an ignition point disguised beside the wiring: a carefully staged fire.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Skull Report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: A fatal fracture caused by a hard, angular object matches the corner of a metal desk in the warehouse office, where signs of cleaning were found.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Owner Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: No booking existed in his name at the "exhibition outside the city" on the night of the disappearance. The gasoline receipt was charged to his card on the very night of the fire.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Guard Interview (After Arrest)
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: He described the argument and the two cans in detail consistent with the physical evidence. He voluntarily took a polygraph test.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Broker Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: The coverage increase followed standard procedures and was initiated by the client. He was a procedural witness, not an accomplice.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Double Ledger Record
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: A secret profit discrepancy worth hundreds of thousands favored the owner. The victim had handwritten a "settling accounts" appointment on the day he disappeared.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Cell Tower Record
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: Rashad's phone connected to the warehouse district tower at 21:40 on the night of the disappearance, not the alleged exhibition.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Office Desk Record
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: The fatal angle matches. Reagents revealed traces of cleaned blood: the original murder scene was the warehouse office itself.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: "Tonight, Everything Will Be Finished" Recording
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: The call at the gas station was to an unidentified person who initially refused to cooperate. He turned out to be a former worker summoned to "help move cabinets." He had declined, narrowly escaping involvement.
strings.reports[0].title: Two Crimes Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: A killing in a moment of anger, followed by a week spent engineering a cover-up: concealment, increased insurance, then fire. The subsequent planning proved more incriminating than the original blow.
strings.reports[1].title: Watch Report
strings.reports[1].author: Trace evidence specialist
strings.reports[1].body: A mechanical watch stopped by impact records the moment of the assault: the most truthful witness in a case whose perpetrator tried to burn every silent witness.
strings.notes[0].text: Here, fire buries rather than kills. Look a week before the fire.
strings.notes[1].text: Who increased the insurance between the disappearance and the fire?
